prompt.context: Our client is a large producer of PET. PET is a type of plastic that is used mainly for producing bottles, such as the ones you find in grocery stores. The main component of PET is PTA. Our client has a PET plant in the US and serves clients both in the US and Europe. They have made the decision to build a PET plant in Europe to be closer to the clients.
prompt.question: They have asked you to evaluate whether they should also backward integrate and purchase a PTA plant and locate both plants next to each other.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost of purchasing the PTA plant?
What is the plant's production capacity?
clarifying_info.a: 1 million metric tons per year, and the plant is producing at capacity

clarifying_info.q: What is the current price of PTA?
What is the cost of the plant and its useful life?
clarifying_info.a: Plant cost is $800MM and it can be used for 50 years

clarifying_info.q: What are the raw material costs?
What are overhead and logistics costs?
Are there any synergies from co-locating the plants?
clarifying_info.a: Overhead savings of $20MM per year and logistics savings of $20 per metric ton

clarifying_info.q: What is the market outlook for PTA prices?
clarifying_info.a: Prices are declining and expected to reach $800 per metric ton in 3 years

exhibits.title: Plant Stand-alone Evaluation & Synergies
exhibits.shows: A structured summary of financial inputs for the PTA plant stand-alone analysis and synergies from backward integration
exhibits.data: Plant purchase cost: $750MM; Capacity: 1M metric tons/year; PTA price: $920/metric ton; Plant cost: $800MM (50-year life); Raw material cost: $690/metric ton; Energy cost: $30/metric ton; Overhead and logistics: $80MM/year; Overhead savings: $20MM/year; Logistics savings: $20/metric ton

exhibits.title: Market Assessment
exhibits.shows: A market assessment section showing the price outlook for PTA over the next three years
exhibits.data: Prices declining; expected to reach $800/metric ton in 3 years

framework: Evaluate the plant on a stand-alone basis (capacity, revenue, fixed costs, variable costs, depreciation, annual profit)
Evaluate synergies from backward integration (overhead savings, logistics savings, incremental annual profit)
Conduct market evaluation and risk assessment (price trends, demand drivers, competitive dynamics)
Synthesize all three components to form a final investment recommendation

questions.prompt: Calculate the annual profit of the PTA plant on a stand-alone basis.
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies all cost components — depreciation (straight-line from plant cost over useful life), variable costs per ton, and fixed overhead — then computes marginal profit per ton and total annual profit.

math.setup: Capacity = 1M mt/year; Price = $920/mt; Raw material = $690/mt; Energy = $30/mt; Overhead & logistics = $80MM/year => $80/mt at capacity; Depreciation = $800MM / 50 years = $16MM/year; Marginal profit per ton = $920 - $690 - $30 - $80 = $120/mt

questions.prompt: Calculate the annual profit of the PTA plant after accounting for synergies from co-location.
questions.guidance: A strong answer adds both synergy streams (overhead savings and logistics savings at capacity) to the stand-alone profit.

math.setup: Overhead savings = $20MM/year; Logistics savings = $20/mt * 1M mt = $20MM/year; Total synergies = $40MM/year

questions.prompt: How does the market outlook affect the investment case? Recalculate annual profit if PTA prices fall to $800/metric ton.
questions.guidance: A strong answer notes that the $120/mt price decline flows directly through to profit at full volume, and that residual profit is largely explained by synergies rather than the plant's intrinsic economics.

math.setup: Price decline = $920 - $800 = $120/mt; Volume = 1M mt; Profit impact = -$120MM

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key risks driving PTA price declines, and what other strategic considerations are relevant to this investment decision?

categories.name: Price / Demand risks
ideas: Imports from cheaper manufacturing countries (e.g., China) increasing supply and compressing prices
Decline in demand driven by increased recycling of plastic bottles
Decline in demand from the 'green' movement in Europe pushing substitution away from single-use plastics
Demand reduction from innovation in product design — bottles requiring less plastic per unit

categories.name: Supply security / strategic benefits
ideas: Backward integration provides guaranteed supply of PTA — though PTA is a commodity so real supply disruption risk is limited
Co-location reduces logistics complexity and dependency on third-party suppliers

categories.name: Financial / valuation risks
ideas: Purchase price of $750MM is high relative to adjusted annual profit of $24MM at stressed prices
At $24MM annual profit the payback period exceeds 30 years — very long for a capital investment
Synergies ($40MM) account for the majority of profitability; stand-alone plant economics are weak under stressed pricing

recommendation: The investment in the PTA plant is difficult to justify at the $750MM purchase price given the market outlook.
At current prices ($920/mt) the plant earns $144MM/year including synergies, suggesting an attractive return, but this is highly sensitive to price declines.

With prices expected to reach $800/mt in 3 years, annual profit falls to only $24MM — of which $40MM comes from synergies, meaning the plant itself is loss-making at stressed prices without co-location benefits.
On balance, the declining price environment and high purchase price make the acquisition unattractive unless the client has high confidence prices will not fall as projected.
risks: PTA prices continue to decline below $800/mt, further eroding returns
Increased imports from low-cost producers (e.g., China) structurally compress margins
Green movement and recycling trends reduce long-run PET/PTA demand in Europe
Synergies may not fully materialize if integration is more complex than projected
next_steps: Commission an independent market study on long-run PTA price trajectory and supply/demand dynamics in Europe
Explore alternative sourcing strategies (long-term supply contracts) as a lower-capital alternative to ownership
Assess whether a lower purchase price could be negotiated to improve the return profile
If proceeding, ensure rigorous integration planning to capture the $40MM in synergies
